subject: FinServe: Follow-up + eval setup (model recommendations & prompt sets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Cara Lin <cara.lin@finserve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-28T15:10:00Z
Subject: FinServe: Follow-up + eval setup (model recommendations & prompt sets)

Hi Cara —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful context on the fraud-detection assistant you’re piloting. Quick recap + next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of needs
- Use case: classify transaction descriptions and generate short rationales for manual review.
- Throughput target: ~500 req/s at 200 tokens/request peak.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms.
- Privacy: PII in inputs; must remain within FinServe VPC or S3 with restricted access.

Model recommendations (initial shortlist)
- mistral-7b-instruct (good instruction-following, cost-efficient for classification + short rationale)
- llm-13b-chat-v2 (higher quality rationales; recommend for a secondary run)
- redwood-instruct-3b-quant (lowest-cost baseline for bulk scoring)

Why these: we balance cost vs. rationale quality. For initial evaluation we suggest running parallel evals: run mistral-7b-instruct as the baseline and llm-13b-chat-v2 for a high-quality comparison.

Eval artifacts we’ll need from you
1) Sample dataset: CSV (see attached redwood_eval_template.csv) with columns: id, input, expected, split (train/dev/test), metadata
2) Metric priorities: precision@k for fraud labels, rationale BLEU/ROUGE-ish for explainability (we’ll also include human spot-check scoring)
3) A few edge-case examples you flagged yesterday (we noted ~20)

Attached: redwood_eval_template.csv (template), redwood-eval-checklist.md (runbook).

Proposed next steps
- You share a sanitized sample CSV (S3 link or attach to email) — we can accept an S3 link with FinServe temporary credentials or you can upload to our secure onboarding bucket.
- We’ll spin up an eval run on Redwood and share a report (model outputs, per-example scores, cost/latency estimates) within 48 hours of dataset receipt.
- Optional: schedule a 30-min deep-dive for results review — propose Tue 2026-05-05 10:00 AM PT.

If that all sounds good I’ll send over a short mutual action plan and request the sample dataset.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed note and the template. This looks right. I attached a small sanitized sample (finserve_sample_eval.csv) — 1,200 rows; dev/test split included. A couple quick questions: 

1) Scoring thresholds: we typically need precision >= 92% on the fraud label for auto-routing to investigators. If models are lower, we’ll keep them in assist mode. Can Redwood score by precision@threshold?

2) PII handling: we prefer the run happen inside our AWS account; can your Eval runner be pointed at our S3 with an IAM role? If not, we’ll share time-limited S3 presigned URLs.

3) Cost: curious on ballpark cost for running both models on the 1.2k dataset.

I’ve cc’d procurement for visibility on any onboarding paperwork.

—Cara

Hi Cara —

Short answers: yes on scoring flexibility, yes on S3-based runs, and ballpark cost below. Details: 

Scoring config
- We can compute precision@threshold and recall@threshold per label. You can set threshold(s) in the eval config (we’ll surface default calibrations then you can override).
- We also support hybrid scoring: combine automatic label score + human review flag to compute a weighted QA score.

Dataset format (required)
- CSV columns (string): id, input, expected, split, metadata
- Example row: 
  id: FSV-0001
  input: "Card purchase at 7-11, $3.45"
  expected: "non-fraud	Rationale: merchant looks normal"
  split: test
  metadata: {"customer_id": "C-1234", "region": "us"}

(We accept JSONL as well; CSV is simplest for your team.)

Cost estimate (very rough)
- mistral-7b-instruct: ~$12 for the full 1.2k run (low-cost baseline)
- llm-13b-chat-v2: ~$65 for the full run (higher-quality rationales)
- Additional human spot-checks (optional): $X/hr depending on reviewer size

Privacy & infra
- We can run evals in your AWS account using an IAM role + S3 input + output buckets. Our onboarding engineer will provide a CloudFormation snippet for minimal permissions (GetObject/PutObject, CloudWatch logs).
- If you'd rather not provide access we can accept presigned upload links that expire after 24 hours.

Next steps from our side
1) If you confirm S3-enable, Marissa will share the CFN/role snippet + onboarding checklist.
2) We’ll load the dataset, run the two models, and present a report with per-example outputs and aggregate metrics in the Redwood Console (link: https://app.redwood.com/evals/FS-2026-0428).

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if you want to walk through the template.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinServe: Follow-up + eval setup (model recommendations & prompt sets)

Cara —

Great, thanks for the sample. We pulled it into a secure onboarding bucket and kicked off the two eval runs. Quick notes and immediate next steps: 

What we ran
- Models: mistral-7b-instruct (baseline) and llm-13b-chat-v2 (high-quality)
- Prompt set: classification prompt + 2-shot rationale template (attached in redwood_eval_template.csv under ‘prompt_examples’ column)
- Scoring config: precision@0.9 and BLEU-like ngram overlap for rationales; human spot-check on 50 random test rows.

Preliminary results (first 200 rows sampled)
- mistral-7b-instruct: precision@0.9 = 88.3% (misses on several edge merchant codes)
- llm-13b-chat-v2: precision@0.9 = 93.6% (better rationale coherence)
- Latency (p95): mistral 7b = 260ms; llm-13b = 480ms (on the Dedicated test pool)

Recommendations
- To meet your 92% precision target for auto-routing, recommend either:
  a) keep mistral as assist + use llm-13b for a high-confidence pass (hybrid), or
  b) fine-tune/calibrate mistral on the 1.2k dev set (we can run 2-shot adaptation + temp scaling)

Next steps
- If you want us to continue, authorize one of the following:
  * Proceed with hybrid pipeline evaluation (we estimate additional cost ~$80).
  * Proceed with quick calibration (2–3 day turnaround).
- We also need SOC2 / SLA details and a signed MSA for Dedicated usage if you want engines inside your VPC. I’ve linked the MSA DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/rv/FS-2026-0428-msa

Scheduling
- I booked the 30-min results review for Tue 2026-05-05 10:00 AM PT — invite should be in your calendar. If that doesn’t work please propose alternate slots.

Attachments included: finserve_sample_eval.csv (your upload), redwood_eval_template.csv, redwood-eval-checklist.md

Thanks — we’ll wait for the authorization selection and confirm the cost estimate once you pick.

Best,
